scope: Characterize the retail handler cluster for s2c 0x018F, 0x0190, and 0x0191, including the 5,569-event 0x0190 route, without promoting imported packet nouns beyond the curated opcode catalog's candidate confidence.
live_capture_status: The current 54-capture sidecar records 5,569 s2c 0x0190 events across eight captures; the four gear captures omit all three opcodes.

method.step1: Cross-reference data/vendor/opcodes/opcodes.json: retail-backed entries remain neutral _0x018F/_0x0190/_0x0191 placeholders; MassSetItemModifierBeginPacket, MassSetItemModifierPacket, and MassSetItemModifierEndPacket are imported candidate labels, not retail-proven nouns.
method.step2: Bulk-decomp FUN_00576CD0 plus cluster (FUN_0076BE60 worker, FUN_00768C40 writer, FUN_00766920 cleanup, FUN_00576C60 + FUN_0076BE30 = 0x18F sibling, FUN_00576D40 + FUN_0076BF10 = 0x191 sibling). 8 functions via DumpFunctionDecomp.java.
method.step3: Identify the 109-byte dispatcher shape (SEH + critical section enter/leave + manager+worker call) shared across all three dispatchers FUN_00576C60/00576CD0/00576D40. FUN_00cc9320 = CS enter, FUN_00cc9330 = CS leave; the manager pointer is *param_1 (the dispatcher arg, a zone-local manager object).
method.step4: Characterize FUN_00768C40 as the record writer: copies 8-byte header (packet[0..1]) to target+0x8/+0xC + zeroes target+0x14/+0x18/+0x1C + allocates 64 bytes via FUN_00783ec0(0x40,0) + copies 16 dwords (64 bytes) from packet[2..18] into *(target+0x14). Total application payload read = 8 + 64 = 72 bytes. The observed 120-byte body includes the 16-byte game-message prefix, leaving a 104-byte application payload and a 32-byte unread tail at +0x48..+0x67.
method.step5: Characterize FUN_00766920 as the record cleanup: conditionally allocates new (FUN_0089B8D0 / FUN_0089BCA0) and conditionally frees old (FUN_00765A90 + _free).
method.step6: Reconcile the equipment-subsystem snapshot: case 399 (0x18F) routes to FUN_00576C60, case 400 (0x190) routes to FUN_00576CD0, and case 401 (0x191) routes to FUN_00576D40.

key_findings: Opcode 0x0190 routes through a per-record update worker between setup-like 0x018F and finalize-like 0x0191 handlers. The current generated pcap sidecar records 5,569 0x0190 events across eight captures.

Wire format: an 8-byte ordered-map key written to record+0x8/+0xC plus a 64-byte record vector copied into a freshly allocated buffer stored at record+0x14. The handler reads 72 bytes of the 104-byte application payload; the 32-byte tail at +0x48..+0x67 is unread and no tail pointer is retained.

The 3 dispatchers FUN_00576C60 / 00576CD0 / 00576D40 share an identical 109-byte shape: critical section enter (FUN_00cc9320 on *param_1) -> worker call -> critical section leave (FUN_00cc9330). The locked object's broader semantic identity remains unresolved.

The 3 workers FUN_0076BE30 / 0076BE60 / 0076BF10 are sized 34 / 168 / 149 bytes. The first performs setup without a data write, the second writes records through FUN_00768C40, and the third runs the finalize path. Begin/Body/End are structural descriptions, not promoted packet names.
Shared helper FUN_0076B950 is called by all 3 workers - probably the manager state-machine validator or transaction step counter. Not separately cataloged (call site is shared infrastructure).
The equipment-subsystem snapshot had 0x018F and 0x0190 swapped. The corrected map is 0x018F -> FUN_00576C60 and 0x0190 -> FUN_00576CD0.

The body, helm, soul, and weapon gear captures contain no 0x018F-0x0191 stream. The earlier full-equipment-swap example is discarded; no retail evidence currently binds this cluster to gear-change frames.
